summary: Intermittent control-plane healthcheck failures due to DNS SRV weight/TTL oscillation in customer split-horizon setup
description:
Issue summary:
FinTrust (private deployment) reports intermittent failures of Redwood control-plane health checks for serving nodes. Failures manifest as transient 'unhealthy' status and short-lived connection rebalances which trigger automatic fallback to older model variants. Impact: production request errors and increased latency for a subset of requests.

Impact:
- ~3-7% of requests during observed windows returned 502/504 or experienced streaming resets tied to node health flapping.
- Customer reports degraded p99 latency and occasional degraded user experience in app telemetry.

Environment:
- Private deployment using VPC Endpoint (VPCE) with split-horizon DNS (internal resolver returns SRV records pointing to internal LB by weight).
- Control-plane healthchecks (gRPC/HTTP) rely on SRV priorities and short TTL for fast failover.

Observed behaviour:
- DNS SRV responses for _redwood-control._tcp.example.internal return varying weights across repeated queries; TTLs observed oscillating between 5s and 180s from the customer's internal resolver cache during the same minute.
- When TTL collapses to 5s and weights flip, the control-plane marks nodes unhealthy until multiple probe retries succeed.

Expected behaviour:
- Stable SRV responses with consistent weights and TTLs consistent with the configured failover policy. Healthchecks should not flap solely due to DNS cache jitter.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From a node in customer VPC, run: dig +short SRV _redwood-control._tcp.example.internal at 1s intervals for 60s
2) Observe SRV weight and target changes along with TTL in responses
3) Trigger a synthetic traffic run that floods a single node (to force health probing and possible reroute) and watch control-plane healthcheck events in the Redwood console
4) Correlate timestamps with customer internal resolver logs and VPCE resolver metrics
logs: 2026-03-12T10:03:17Z resolver: SRV _redwood-control returned 3 entries with weights [100,0,0] ttl=5s
2026-03-12T10:03:21Z resolver: SRV _redwood-control returned 3 entries with weights [0,100,0] ttl=180s
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: split-horizon resolver returning inconsistent SRV weights due to internal orchestration (service discovery) churn and low TTLs causing cache thrash at VPCE resolver.

Customer confirmed they run an internal service registry that republishes SRV records with aggressive TTLs to accelerate failovers for their own services. We observed TTLs toggling between 5s and 180s corresponding to registry refresh events.

Control-plane healthchecks are sensitive to DNS SRV order/weight because our routing selection evaluates DNS weight at each probe when TTL is low. Rapid weight oscillation can cause our healthcheck to consider the endpoint unstable for the duration of probe retries.
Reproduced in lab by emulating SRV responses with varying TTLs using dnsmasq: when TTL<=5s and weights alternate, healthcheck state transitions occur within 10-30s matching customer behaviour.
VPCE local cache observed dropping entries on low TTL which triggers new upstream queries; internal registry momentarily returned different weight assignments during leader election windows.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support): Received initial report and validated Redwood console health flaps. Asked customer for resolver query logs and SRV dig outputs.

Customer (FinTrust SRE - Marco Rossi): Attached dig outputs showing frequent weight flips correlated with their internal deployment pipeline (canary rollout job runs every minute). Confirmed no firewall drops or packet loss.

Daniel Kim (Infra SRE): Reproduced locally using dnsmasq + scripted SRV toggles; healthchecks flip after second probe failure. Proposed mitigation: treat SRV weight changes within a short window as noise and add a small debounce in healthcheck logic OR recommend customer increase TTL to >=30s during canary churn.
Aisha Patel (Support): Asked product/infra teams to evaluate safety of debouncing weight changes for private deployments. Escalated to networking/serving-runtime for impact analysis.
Product Lead (Maya Li): Requested a risk assessment for changing healthcheck semantics; asked for telemetry on how many private customers use SRV split-horizon with sub-10s TTLs.
resolution: Workaround: Customer increased SRV TTL to 60s in their service registry during an initial mitigation window; after TTL increase, control-plane health flaps stopped and p99 latency returned to baseline. Long-term fix options: (A) Implement a conservative debounce in control-plane SRV-weight handling to ignore weight-only changes within a short window (default 15s) for private deployments; (B) Document recommended SRV TTL/weight patterns in Private Deployment runbook. Action items: INT-442 create feature proposal for debounce; SUP-608007 to remain open until code review and rollout plan or final runbook published.
